protocol.instrument_name: Protocol for Resupply of the Oral Contraceptive Pill - Tasmanian Pharmacist Initiative
protocol.instrument_version: Version 2.0 (cover: 'Version 2.0 May 2025'; version history: 'V 2.0 May 2025 ... Legislative change'; 'V1.0 March 2024 ... Original Protocol')
protocol.effective_date: May 2025 (cover and version history); authority table records authorisation by Dale Webster, Secretary, Department of Health on 4 June 2025
protocol.legal_basis: Tasmanian Poisons Regulations 2018 Regulation 7 (Relevant Legislation, page 5): '(4) A pharmacist, in the lawful practice of the pharmacist's profession, may possess, sell, supply or prescribe any scheduled substance in accordance with a protocol authorised by the Secretary, that specifically authorises the possession, sale, supply or prescription of that substance by a pharmacist. This protocol has been endorsed by the Secretary.' Authorisation Statement (page 2): 'In accordance with Tasmanian Poisons Regulations 2018 Regulation 7(4) - I authorise this protocol.' (Dale Webster, Secretary). Purpose (page 4): 'It is a regulatory requirement under the Tasmanian Poison Regulations 2018 that pharmacists follow this protocol under a structured prescribing arrangement.' Background (page 4): 'The Tasmanian Poisons Legislation allows pharmacists to supply medications included in this protocol.' Prescribing Considerations (page 9): 'Any prescription needs to comply with Regulation 45 of the Poisons Regulations 2018 which outlines the elements needed to produce a valid prescription in Tasmania.'
protocol.supervision_model: Structured prescribing arrangement (Glossary, page 5: 'prescribing specific medications for a specified purpose in accordance with a protocol published by the Tasmanian Department of Health'). Participating pharmacists 'must only offer this structured prescribing service in a pharmacy premises that has been approved by the Department of Health' (Pharmacy premises approved for the UTI pilot have their approval grandfathered for OCP resupply), must be 'currently AHPRA registered and have evidence of completion of a training course approved by the Department of Health' (Purpose, page 4), and must satisfy the five Mandatory Requirements (page 4).
protocol.scope_summary: Tasmanian Department of Health protocol allowing pharmacists to resupply the oral contraceptive pill for up to 12 months under a structured prescribing arrangement. Sequential flowchart (pages 6-8): age 16-50; OCP on the protocol medicines list; initiated by GP/other authorised prescribing health care professional and stabilised on that pill for 2 years continuously; GP review of the OCP in the last two years; continuous OCP use (pill-break rules, page 10); consent to a private consult with the pharmacist present; patient-needs assessment (pregnancy/breastfeeding, counselling incl. LARCs, reproductive health enquiry, STI screening referral); clinical review (My Health Record, BP, BMI, smoking, new medicines, pregnancy planning); contraindication screen (all-OCP box plus COC-only box) with 'Prompt referral to General Practitioner or other health service'. Positive branch issues a prescription and repeats (max 12-month supply; 40-50 year olds on COC limited to one original pack and one repeat), with separate dispensing, preventative health advice and plan communication. Appendices 1 (pages 15-16) list UKMEC category 3/4 contraindications and 'other conditions that require immediate referral' for COCP and POP. Only two pill types are authorised: combined oral contraceptive pill (COCP) and progestogen-only pill (POP or mini pill).

steps.description: 'Examination - The pharmacist should measure BP and calculate BMI to determine the person's suitability for continuing their OCP. A single elevated BP reading is not enough to classify a patient as hypertensive (e.g. also take into consideration activity immediately prior to consultation) and a second BP reading should be taken at the end of the consultation. If BP remains elevated, the patient should be referred to a medical practitioner for further assessment and selection of an appropriate contraceptive method.'

gates.criterion: BP is not elevated on the second reading taken at the end of the consultation

provenance.pdf_file: tas-pharmacist-prescribing-protocols\Protocoal for Resupply of the Oral Contraceptive Pill_1.pdf

steps.description: 'Patient History - Sufficient information must be obtained from the patient to assess the safety and appropriateness of any recommendations and medicines, including resupply of the OCP, for the patient. Review MHR where available and appropriate. Consider: Age; Pregnancy and breastfeeding status; Underlying medical conditions, including new or recently diagnosed medical conditions, which may: be a contraindication to hormonal contraception e.g. migraine with aura, impact on contraceptive effectiveness and choice; Current medications, including check adherence and satisfaction with OCP; Drug allergies/adverse effects, including any adverse effects of OCP; Smoking status (there is an increased VTE risk in smokers over 35 years); BMI; Last STI screen and Cervical Screening Test (CST)*; Presence of genitourinary symptoms that may suggest STI: Changes in vaginal or urethral discharge, Vulval, genital skin problems or symptoms, Lower abdominal pain, Dysuria, HPV vaccination status. '* All patients seeking contraception who have not had a CST in the previous 5 years should be advised to see a medical practitioner for a CST, and a referral provided if the patient consents. They are still eligible to receive a resupply of the Pill.'

steps.description: '14. Confirm OCP Resupply/Contraception Plan is Appropriate - Pharmacists must consult the Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook and other relevant references to confirm the OCP is appropriate for the patient, including for: Contraindications and precautions; Drug interactions; Pregnancy and lactation.'

steps.description: 'Excluding Pregnancy - If the patient is still taking the OCP and there are no symptoms or signs of pregnancy, they can be reasonably assumed not to be pregnant. However, if there is any doubt regarding whether the patient may be pregnant, the patient should be advised to take a pregnancy test and provided this is negative, they may then return to the pharmacy for the resupply of their OCP.'

gates.criterion: No doubt about pregnancy (still taking the OCP with no symptoms or signs of pregnancy), or a negative pregnancy test where doubt exists

provenance.pdf_file: tas-pharmacist-prescribing-protocols\Protocoal for Resupply of the Oral Contraceptive Pill_1.pdf

steps.description: '16. Communicate Agreed Plan for OCP Resupply - Offering comprehensive counselling that covers adverse effects, instructions for use and patient expectations where this is required assists to promote effective and ongoing contraceptive use. Comprehensive advice and counselling (including supporting written information when required) as per the Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook, UKMEC 2016, and other relevant references, should be provided to the patient regarding: Individual product and medicine use; Managing missed pills and emergency contraception options available if required; How to manage adverse effects; When to seek further care and/or treatment: The signs of VTE and what to do if it is suspected; The importance of reporting new or worsening mood-related symptoms to the pharmacist and usual medical practitioner.'

steps.description: '17. Follow Up - Pharmacists should advise the patient that they can seek a resupply of their OCP at the pharmacy of their choice when they next need a replacement pack (approximately four months later depending on OCP pack size). It is recommended that: The patient's BP should be monitored at 12 monthly intervals, and Patients should be reviewed by their GP at least every 2 years.'

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'The protocol will not cover all possible clinical circumstances and pharmacists are required to exercise their professional judgement in adapting the treatment guideline to individual circumstances.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Open-ended professional-judgement clause; needs a local policy boundary before enforcement by a rules engine.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Short-term bridging supply: 'In circumstances where a pharmacist determines that ongoing resupply is not suitable but a significant risk of unplanned pregnancy without ongoing supply is present, a short-term supply may be considered until an appointment is able to be secured with a GP or other health service.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: 'May be considered' with no quantity, duration or approval criteria printed; local policy must define limits (e.g. one pack, max weeks).

hugh_to_confirm.item: Prescription formalities: 'Any prescription needs to comply with Regulation 45 of the Poisons Regulations 2018 ... Electronic prescribing templates may be used provided they meet the requirements of Reg 45 and are signed in ink by the pharmacist. Pharmacists are to indicate the words "authorised health professional" after signature and name on the prescription. The original prescription is to accompany the repeats and the pharmacy is to establish a process to retain a copy of the original prescription on file.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Local prescribing workflow and template configuration must be validated against Reg 45 before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Premises approval: 'Participating pharmacists must only offer this structured prescribing service in a pharmacy premises that has been approved by the Department of Health. Pharmacy premises that have already been approved for the UTI pilot project are able to have their approval grandfathered for the OCP resupply initiative.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Approval status must be confirmed per site (and grandfathering evidenced).

hugh_to_confirm.item: Approved training courses: 'Pharmaceutical Society of Australia - Contraception Essentials' and 'Australasian College of Pharmacy (Tasmania) - Contraceptives: a comprehensive training course for pharmacists' (page 5) / 'Oral contraceptives: a comprehensive training course for pharmacists' and 'Contraception Essentials Explained' (page 4); section header incorrectly says the courses are for 'urinary tract infections'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Course names differ between pages and the header is inconsistent; verify each pharmacist's certificate against the current approved list.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Dispensing separation: 'Dispensing process is to be performed separately from prescribing (for example: physically move from consult room into the dispensary)' plus 'Best practice advice: wherever available, another pharmacy staff member should be involved in the dispensing process. A pharmacist (first-preference) or a dispense tech.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Physical workflow requirement plus 'best practice advice' (not mandatory); local policy must define compliance evidence.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Pill-break judgement: 'If a patient frequently takes pill breaks, pharmacists should exercise their professional judgement and consider referring the patient to explore alternative contraception options, e.g., long-acting reversible contraception (LARCs).'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: 'Frequently' is undefined and the referral is optional; local rule required.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Child protection reporting: 'Pharmacists are to consider whether there may be child protection concerns relating to a request for contraception and report to Child Protection accordingly by contacting the Strong Families, Safe Kids advice and referral line on 1800 000 123...'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Mandatory-reporting judgement with no printed threshold; encoded as a REFER red flag because the schema has no report action - local policy must define the decision path.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Capacity/consent for patients under 18: 'Consent ... may be provided by either the: parent or legal guardian; patient (must be assessed as having capacity ...)' and 'A child or young person's capacity can be observed and assessed by a pharmacist on a case-by-case basis.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Capacity assessment is a case-by-case judgement; local documentation standard required.

hugh_to_confirm.item: External reference currency: 'the current versions of the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists Faculty of Sexual and Reproductive Healthcare (FSRH) documentation, including: UK Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use 2016 (UKMEC); FSRH Clinical Guideline: Progestogen-only Pills (August 2022, Amended July 2023); FSRH Clinical Guideline: Combined Hormonal Contraception (January 2019, Amended July 2023)' and 'Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook and other relevant references'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Rules depend on external, versioned references; confirm which versions the module pins at go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Age 40-50 COC supply limit: 'eligible for maximum of one original pack and one repeat' / 'one original pack and one repeat only' plus '†12 months can be supplied for progestogen-only pills.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Quantity limits must be configured in the prescribing/dispensing system, and the dagger footnote's scope must be resolved (see open_questions).

hugh_to_confirm.item: Contraindication screen completeness: flowchart box is abbreviated ('*Please refer to Appendix 1 for full set of contraindications to resupply') and Appendix 1 states its list is 'not an exhaustive list' and is based on UKMEC/Therapeutic Guidelines.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The engine cannot rely on the printed lists alone; confirm the intended live source of truth (UKMEC calculator / Therapeutic Guidelines) and how it is version-pinned.

hugh_to_confirm.item: First-line COCP footnote: '* NB: first-line choice of COCP is a monophasic formulation containing ethinylestradiol (20 or 30 micrograms) and levonorgestrel (Therapeutic Guidelines)'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: First-line designation is delegated to an external guideline; confirm the exact product list used for 'first-line' prompts.

hugh_to_confirm.item: BP second-reading rule: 'If BP remains elevated, the patient should be referred to a medical practitioner...' - no threshold printed for 'elevated'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: A numeric rule cannot be implemented without a threshold; confirm whether 140/90 mmHg (contraindication box) is the intended trigger or another value.

hugh_to_confirm.item: My Health Record review: 'Review My Health Record, where available' and consent for 'Access to the patient's My Health Record for checking relevant medical history'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Depends on local system access and patient consent arrangements.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Service scope: 'Under the initiative, Tasmanian pharmacies are only authorised to resupply two types of oral hormonal contraceptive pills: the combined oral contraceptive pill (COCP) and the progestogen only pill (POP or mini pill)' and 'COCPs with a high estrogen dose (50 micrograms of ethinylestradiol or equivalent) ... have been excluded from this initiative.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Product-level allow/deny list must be maintained against the printed table (including the unresolved estrogen-dose cells) before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Documentation minimum set (page 9) and 'The pharmacist must make a clinical record of the consultation that contains at a minimum: ...' plus consultation-summary sharing rules.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Local clinical software must be configured to capture every listed element, including consent items.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Protocol review cycle: 'This protocol will be updated every two years or more frequently as required.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Version pinning: confirm the module runs against v2.0 (May 2025) and has a re-verification trigger on republication.
